About concepts and catalog references

Future item concepts are fictional prompts for possible game content; they have no current-game stats, rules, or compatibility. Current catalog references come from exported item text. Similar wording is only a lead for designers to review, not proof of synergy, slot legality, balance, or gameplay performance.

Cross-class comparison · Content · Role

CONTENT PATHS.

Compare class build paths for the same content and role. Each path shows core-skill item candidates and source-text gaps, so you can see where a creative build has catalog support to investigate.

Reading supportPrimary = proposed best-fit content · Eligible = proposed possible fit. Item matches are candidates from catalog text; coverage does not prove build legality or combat performance.
Class freedom · Build paths · Catalog support

CLASS PATHS.

Explore every class through its candidate build paths, core skills and item support. Matches are theorycraft candidates based on source text, not confirmed compatibility. Missing links highlight skills worth reviewing so each class can develop a distinct, playable identity.

How to use this pageOpen a class to see its build paths. Open a build to review each skill’s weapon, card, Tome and Sigil candidates, then explore candidates in the planner.
How item matches and gaps are identified

Candidate matches use exact skill names or meaningful words from a skill name in exported item text; Tome related-skill references are treated as explicit links. “No item match” means the export contains no matching text for that skill. It does not prove there is no useful item. Item slot, class legality, stat scaling and combat performance still require review in the full builder.

Data Coverage & Reliability

No global player leaderboard is inferred from Codex candidates. Only imported combat records can inform observed performance. Synthetic records remain clearly identified and are excluded from factual balance claims. Sampling bias, gear differences, encounters, player skill, role and patch changes require review before balancing.
